name: Trivia Bluff
description: Round by round, an obscure real fact with a blank. Students write believable lies to fill it, then everyone votes for the truth among the fakes. Points for spotting the truth, points for every classmate your lie fools. The facts are yours: written by you, or found for you in encyclopedia articles on a topic, each with the sentence it came from, so you can check every one before class.
tagline: A bluffing game: everyone writes a believable fake, then hunts for the true answer among them. It gets sharper with every round.

default.question: The Roman emperor Augustus prohibited serving legionaries from ___, a decree that stayed in force for two centuries.
Because of their size, the males of the African driver ant are called "___".
In 1885 the German writer Heinrich Böhnke-Reich warned against using old ___ as coffee filters.

questions.label: The facts
questions.helper: Each is a sentence with a blank shown as ___ plus the real answer. The decoy is an optional extra wrong choice to mix in with student lies. One round per fact.

question.label: Fact with a blank
question.placeholder: The mayor of Rabbit Hash, Kentucky is a ___.

lieTimer.label: Lie-writing time (seconds)
lieTimer.helper: How long students get to write their fake answer each round.

template.name: Trivia Bluff
template.description: A fact with a blank and believable lies. Pick the truth to score; fool the class to score too.

intro.message:
TRIVIA BLUFF!

You'll see an obscure fact with a blank. Write a believable lie to fill it in. The class will then try to spot the truth, but your lie might fool them!

qlies${i}.prompt:
${item.question}

Write a lie that could fool the class.

qreveal${i}.message:
The truth was: ${item.truth}!

What the class picked:
{{qvote${i}.barChart}}

Liars, own up! Whose lie pulled the most votes?

end.message: That's Trivia Bluff! 100 for spotting the truth, 50 per classmate fooled. Run it again with fresh facts.
